long_description:
Up! Go! More! is a bright, uncluttered first-words book for babies and toddlers, built for laps, not screens. Each of its 22 pages shows one everyday word a little one really uses, from hi and peekaboo to eat, help, more, all done and night-night. The word is set in huge rounded letters above one big, friendly picture.

Every page also gives you two small things to do together. A Say it, Sign it or Act it cue offers one sound, simple hand sign or move to copy, like tapping fingertips for more or hiding your eyes for peekaboo. A short grown-up tip turns reading into a back-and-forth chat: pause and wait, add one word, offer a choice, copy each other, or follow your child's lead. There is no script and nothing to get right. Pick any tip and skip any tip.

The front pages explain how to read together in four plain steps. The back pages show where the words live in your day, from mealtime to bedtime, and include a keepsake word list, pages to add your family's own words, and a free printable bonus for grown-ups.

Up! Go! More! is Book 1 of the Talk-Along Firsts series. Next come sounds and animals, then routines and feelings.
bullets: 22 real first words, one per page: hi, peekaboo, up, down, go, stop, ball, in, open, wow, uh-oh, help, clap, shoe, eat, cup, more, all done, bye-bye, book, hug, night-night
A Say it, Sign it or Act it cue on every page: one sound, simple hand sign or move for you and your little one to copy together
A grown-up tip on every page with one easy talk idea: wait, add a word, offer a choice, copy each other, follow their lead
Huge rounded letters and one big, bold, uncluttered picture per page, with an inclusive cast of toddlers, parents and grandparents

compliance_notes: No health or medical claims: this is a parent-education picture book, not a treatment or professional service of any kind, and it claims no outcome for any child. It is not presented as written by a speech-language professional, and no diagnosis or condition is named or targeted in its text, keywords or ads (BRAND.md hard rule 1 and the diagnosis-search rule). Talk strategies are described in plain words, with no trademarked program names. No real brands, logos, schools or products; the tablet on the night-night page is a generic, neutral object. No research citations are used. Hand signs are described as simple signs, not as a sign-language course. The inside pages say that every child talks on their own timeline and point parents to their child's doctor with questions. Safety: no small objects are suggested (blocks, a ball, a cup and a duck toy only; no food choking hazards) and adult reading together is assumed. The paperback has paper pages, so the listing says 'read together'.
